title: Senior Business Analyst, Product Development
description: # **Senior Business Analyst, Product Development** ### **About the product** Most companies still answer business questions the way they did twenty years ago. Someone files a request, an analyst turns it into SQL, and the answer arrives after the decision has moved on. We build an AI analytics platform that ends that wait. A business user asks a question in plain English and gets a correct, charted answer from their organisation's data in seconds, along with the anomalies, forecasts and recommended actions they never thought to ask for. Every answer the AI gives is only as good as the business definitions sitting behind it. ### **The role** You join the product development team, the engineers and analysts who build the platform itself. You own the backlog, turn what clients and the market need into requirements a developer can build from, and decide with the team what earns a place on the roadmap. It is a business analysis role with one difference. The product you specify is an AI. When the output is a button you can write the acceptance criteria in a line. When the output is an answer a model generates, you have to define what correct looks like, design the tests that prove it, and turn every miss into something an engineer can reproduce and fix. You do the data work yourself, and when a number looks wrong you are the one who finds out why. ### **What you'll work on** - Own the backlog with our developers, the stories, acceptance criteria and testing, and what earns a place on the roadmap. - Turn client needs, implementation team feedback and your own product judgment into requirements a developer can build from. - Define what correct looks like for AI features, the acceptance criteria for answers, charts and dashboards that a model generates rather than a template renders. - Design and run the acceptance and regression tests for each release, grading the AI's answers against the actual data, and turn every miss into a precise, reproducible issue. - Query the data yourself whenever a definition or a number is in doubt. Nobody hands you a data dictionary. - Shape the product's semantic foundations, the measures, filters and business terms the platform reasons with. - Test and iterate dashboards and new visualisation capabilities as they ship. - Join key client sessions to see the product in real use, and bring what you learn back to the roadmap. ### **What we're looking for** - A senior track record in business analysis, product ownership and data analytics, with real depth in all three. - Strong SQL, and hands-on Microsoft Fabric or a platform you would carry across quickly. - You can take raw data and a vaguely worded business question and get to the answer yourself, in the database. - Experience owning a backlog alongside developers on a product that is still changing underneath you. - You write requirements and acceptance criteria with the precision of someone who knows both an engineer and a machine will read them. - AI-assisted ways of working used in real delivery rather than tried once. - You can hold your own with executive stakeholders when you join client sessions ### **Nice to have** Semantic or metric layer work, Python, UAT or QA practice, Power BI, experience testing or evaluating AI products, and early-stage delivery. ### **How we work** Small senior team, remote, working directly with the engineers who ship your requirements. The product is young and moving, so you will define the method and ship against fixed dates at the same time. If that reads as freedom rather than chaos, we should talk. _**Note:** This is a Remote job, with office visits on request. Some client meetings fall in US hours._

title: Lead AI Engineer
description: # **Lead AI Engineer** ### **About the product** Most companies still answer business questions the way they did twenty years ago. Someone files a request, an analyst turns it into SQL, and the answer arrives after the decision has moved on. We build an AI analytics platform that ends that wait. A business user asks a question in plain English and gets a correct, charted answer from their organisation's data in seconds, along with the anomalies, forecasts and recommended actions they never thought to ask for. The platform is in production with enterprise clients across industries. ### **The role** You own the AI core, the agents that turn a business question into a correct answer. That covers the architecture, the models, the prompts, the knowledge the agents reason over, and the evaluation that tells you whether an answer is right. Most of your time goes into designing and writing code, and the rest into the calls that shape the product. This is a hands-on staff-level position. You report to some of the leading global experts in the field, set the technical direction for the AI core, and carry the hardest problems yourself. ### **What you'll work on** - Build and evolve the agent runtime, an orchestrator that plans multi-step analyses, runs queries in parallel, spawns sub-agents and hands off to domain specialists, spanning quick streamed answers and long-running deep investigations. - Own the query generation. The agents translate natural language into T-SQL and DAX over messy enterprise schemas, backed by deterministic query patterns and a governed metric layer for the questions where roughly right is not good enough. - Design the knowledge the agents reason over, including the ontology and knowledge graph that describe a client's schema, entities, business rules and vocabulary, the semantic and metric layer above it, and the retrieval that brings the right piece forward at the right moment. - Push the platform from answering to anticipating, growing the proactive side of the product. Anomaly detection, clustering, forecasting and recommended actions should reach the user before the question is asked. - Engineer for speed and cost, with model tiering across agent roles, prompt cache economics, streaming, parallelism and tracing that shows where every millisecond and cent goes. - Keep change safe with golden question corpora, LLM-judged scoring backed by deterministic checks, release gates in CI and variant experiments when a new model ships. - Enforce security inside the agent, from row-level security applied to generated queries to tool gating, schema pruning and prompt injection defence - Open new domains. You make each new industry a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild. ### **What we're looking for** - A senior track record in AI engineering, with recent years spent shipping LLM-based systems that real users depend on, not prototypes. - Hands-on depth with agent architectures, covering orchestration, tool use, structured outputs, multi-step planning and the failure modes that come with them. - Strong SQL and genuine comfort inside a data warehouse. When the agent gives a wrong answer, you can trace it through the prompt, the query and the schema to the root cause. - Experience building the knowledge side of AI systems, whether ontologies, knowledge graphs, semantic layers or retrieval pipelines, and clear opinions on when each is the right tool - You have built eval suites for nondeterministic systems and used them to ship changes with confidence. - You can build the predictive side of the product, anomaly detection, clustering and forecasting that hold up on real data, and you know when a simple statistical method beats a model. - Production-grade Python, async services, streaming APIs and the discipline to keep a growing system understandable. - The range to set technical direction and still write the hardest code yourself. ### **Nice to have** Microsoft Fabric or Power BI and DAX, the Azure ecosystem, vector stores such as pgvector, LLM observability and cost tooling, multi-tenant SaaS, enough TypeScript to read the dashboard frontend, and early-stage product delivery. ### **How we work** Small senior team, remote, with direct access to the end clients and the problems they need solved. The product is young and moving, so you will define the method and ship against fixed dates at the same time. If that reads as freedom rather than chaos, we should talk. _**Note:** This is a Remote job, with office visits on request. Some client meetings fall in US hours._

title: Senior Data Engineer, Client Implementations

Everything the AI knows about a client's business flows from the data platform underneath it. ### **The Role** You join the implementation team, the people who take a new client from a won deal to a live deployment. You sit in the client sessions, work out their business and data requirements, take receipt of their raw source data, and build the medallion architecture the deployment runs on. Your warehouse has an unusual consumer. It is read by an AI agent thousands of times a day, without a human in the loop, and every ambiguity you leave in the model can surface as a confident wrong answer in a chat window. You build data models a language model can read correctly, and that is a higher bar than building for people. ### **What you'll work on** - Join client meetings from kickoff, with their operations people and their IT, and turn what the business means by its own terms into definitions a pipeline can compute. - Take raw source extracts, CRM systems, operational feeds and event logs, and work out their structure, grain and quality yourself. Client data dictionaries are rare and usually wrong. - Build the bronze, silver and gold layers, from ingestion through transform notebooks to a governed gold star schema, with incremental loads, watermarks and freshness you can vouch for. - Encode the client's business logic in the transforms. Typical cases include current state that must be derived from an audit event log with carry-forward rules, identity resolution across parent and child records, and exclusion rules that change what every downstream count means. - Write the data dictionary that feeds the agent, the table and column annotations, grain cards and join paths that become part of what the AI knows about the client. - Prove the numbers are right. Reconcile the gold layer against the client's source reports, run the data-quality , chase every figure that does not tie, and fix the transform rather than the symptom. - Design the row-level security model at the data layer, so the same warehouse serves different user scopes safely. - Make each new client faster than the last, hardening the ingestion and modelling playbook so onboarding becomes repeatable. ### **What we're looking for** - A senior track record in data engineering, with warehouses or lakehouses you built running in production and being relied on. - Expert SQL and strong Python, including PySpark or a similar large-scale transform stack. - Real depth in dimensional modelling. You think in grains, conformed dimensions and slowly changing state, and you can derive current state correctly from an event log. - You are comfortable in front of a client. You can sit with business stakeholders, ask the questions that surface what they actually mean, and hold your own when their numbers disagree with yours. - A reconciliation habit. You have owned the correctness of a data platform, you assume the numbers do not tie until proven otherwise, and you have the patience to find out why. - You can take an undocumented source system and map it yourself, without waiting for someone to explain it. ### **Nice to have** Microsoft Fabric or Delta Lake, the Azure ecosystem, complex CRM or operational source systems, dbt or a similar transform framework, data-quality tooling, Power BI, and experience feeding data to LLM or ML systems. ### **How we work** Small senior team, remote, with direct access to the end clients and the problems they need solved. The product is young and moving, so you will define the method and ship against fixed dates at the same time.
